content:
" They say that, whenever you see the stars fall, if you wish upon them to live, you’ll get to see next morning’s sun. "Even long after the war the stories of a monster so precise, so reckless, that hunted those foolish enough to venture into the forest at night stayed. Though now it was nothing but a myth that few remembered where it originated from, some swore it still held true.
And Ant hated it. Hated what it meant because he would never forget it, because it forever tainted his very being. But it was useful. People expected to meet a reckless monster, and he didn’t want to be found, so keeping them at bay through fear was effective. However, he rarely brought himself to display any aggressiveness, his strong build and sharp features where more than enough to scare anyone away. Well, almost anyone.
Extra notes#I was thinking of Ant at work and I kept picturing him, standing on his own in the middle of the night, so his people can sleep peacefully. Pushing the enemy lines back and keeping them at bay while the sun is down. His blindness becoming a tactical advantage as he doesn’t rely on light to see. While his fire magic, polished to be more of an spectacle than an attack, falls in form of stars that temporarily blind those who dare get close enough, and in the worst cases, even burn them. Not fully of course, but enough to scare and sometimes scar.
summary: A short exploration of the nights during the monster war.
title: Starry nights [Ant]

content:
He curls into himself, memories becoming foggy as he forgets about who he is, or rather who he was pretending to be, no longer responding to the very name he set for himself. An invisible weight lifts off from his shoulders, a weight he once grew so accustomed to, but that now seems completely senseless. He slowly unfolds, finding something in his new form that felt nostalgic. Having rediscovered himself he looks back at the bowtie in his hand, no longer recognizing it as his own he discards it.Cino#From succino, one of the names for amber in spanish. I chose that because of its usual warm yellow hues, but also because it conserves ancient life, as the transformation uncovers Kayden’s past self (Raylen, that’s what the R stands for).
Lemon shark: social, known for their docile approach to humans. They also prefer a stalking style of hunting. He may seem like he got more colder because of his default poker face but he’s gotten more social, clingy even. He’s a great listener, though paired with his more silent demeanour he might seem a little stalk-y. He’s just the type to observe his surroundings a lot. A little shy, even untrusting with strangers, but easily bonds to whoever pays attention to him. Having his size no longer hindered he’s not only grown back to his full height but even gotten a little bigger reaching 4m (13 ft). He will silently judge you but will also keep it to himself unless provoked. Design notes#The modifications are based on external controller modifications, they wrap around and integrate into his body being a similar hard plastic-like material. Image references used for Cino’s design.He’s expressionless by default. When he does show his mouth a couple fangs are always seen. But what about the pub#That’s a good question i answer to nobody. A question i’m not too sure about lol I have like a couple takes:
The place tries to hold him hostage, but as his very being has changed he can take the opportunity to escape unscathed. Though going back in there is a really bad idea. The place no longer recognizes him and is essentially freed from that contract. The third most evil version is that the place just straight up punishes him before kicking him out. But I’m not sure how this would go (it wouldn’t be the same as the excerpt I wrote… or maybe yes? 🤔)
summary: After breaking a certain contract Kayden has to face the consecuences.
title: Cino [Shark!Kayden]

content:
Already deeply hurt by the abandonmnet, the abuse and missuse fully breaks Kayden, remaking himself from the ground up.First sketches of Null!Kayden.I think i don’t take enough into account that R. Kayden is actually pretty well taken care of! It kind of relates to his desire to offer the best of himself all the time. The null! version of him explores to how different he ends up beeing after receiving the completely oposite treatment:
For starters, there’s the physical evidence of damage, keeping his screen on is straining for him hence why he defaults to have it shut off. Can’t really pick up signals so he is only of use connected to things like consoles: This makes him much less hesitant to adapt to the newer tech, whatever helps him be a little more of use is welcomed. He is really rough on himself, doesn’t take failure kindly, and he holds those high standards to the rest (even if he doesn’t show it at first). I mean. Original Kay also does this but in this case it’s more extreme. Somehow more on edge than normal Kay -> sharp teeth are on always. Doesn’t fear the new tech tho, he’s got an RCA to HDMI adapter and mocap gloves Has polished his game modifying abilities to make them more addictive to players -> possible control thing…? Lost his whimsy, games are now just a means to an end 😔 More of a “serious” butler in a sense, but the kind to poison everyone and get away with it Fake ass mf , also a fake it till you make it pro Bad tendency to see others as stepping stones. However he will always try to get to their good side, and gets annoyed when they dislike him. Kind of a “with me or against me” mentality. Doesn’t deny himself what he wants, at most he just postpones it. Much more forward, though less loyal.
summary: After so much time alone, Kayden is welcomed to a new home. Not a kind one, but he perseveres.
title: Null!Kayden

content:
In short, it’s a Monster Tenna story based on Undertale but set in a more modernized world, and it reinterprets the war and some aspects of it. It’s also loosely based on the Legend of Hei (especially the theme of the battle between spirits and humans). The years don’t match to irl events but its based on that for like technological reference points and such, like when Ant starts his career is around 1950-ish. Also he’s a boss monster and that aging logic applies.
Timeline#Ant’s story is divided into three parts, with the war between humans and monsters serving as the common thread.
Before the War#Before the war, Ant worked in entertainment. He was born into a prominent family of insectoid monsters, a family that had always been very sociable. But Ant was the first to delve deeper into the human world, fascinated by their art, especially their music, and by the fact that they used sounds rather than magic to enhance their performances, since Ant was born blind, just like his mother.
His affable and friendly demeanour, paired with his natural charisma, quickly earned him a good reputation in the industry, and he eventually went on to host his own children’s shows aimed at educating both humans and monsters. He believed this would help bridge the social divide between the two over time. During this time, he met many people and even travelled around the world; it was a very hectic period where he was always on edge, but he enjoyed the intensity of it all and how much he could learn about human culture.
However, all this fame threatened to vanish overnight. At first, not quite sure why, he frantically reached out to everyone he knew, searching for an explanation. No one could give him an answer until a mysterious but charming man, short in stature but with a great personality, named Spencer explained which trends he should follow to maintain his popularity. This was a huge help, as thanks to him the studio managed to stay afloat, but the audience still wasn’t what it used to be. Human-monster relations, due to various political tensions, were on a steady decline.
Ant, aware of this, pleaded one last time to Spencer for information. The human, terrified and worried for Ant due to the increasingly real threat of war, tried to uncover the details of how the war would begun. In that very last attempt to obtain intelligence, and despite his informant and benefactor’s warning, he was caught red-handed and deemed a spy against humanity.
During the War#The monster, now with his closest companion gone and the studio in ruins, had to retreat to live in a village, taken in by old friends, both humans and monsters. They gave him a home, and in return, he did what he did best: entertaining and educating the children, shielding them from the danger lurking in more distant cities and the tension this caused among the adults.
The war eventually reached even that remote town, and Ant, despite being a boss monster of considerable power, was unable to strike back at the humans, instead focusing on defending the children, the monsters, and the other humans who stayed behind to fight alongside him. However, that wasn’t enough, and he was eventually overwhelmed by firearms. He was rescued and saved by the very children he was protecting, who, with the support of their parents, hid him in a shed and helped stabilize him with weak healing magic.
Even after such a fierce battle, the monsters were forced to abandon the surface, tearing apart many relationships, including entire families from that village. But it was a gradual process. Although a large number retreated that very day, just as many were driven out later or even managed to remain on the surface. Some went into hiding or sought refuge among sympathetic humans, but their nature made this a difficult task. So much so that many monsters on the surface eventually turned themselves in of their own accord, unable to live in the shadows and the constant threat to be hunted.
After the War#However, Ant was unable to leave the village. It lay completely destroyed and abandoned, no one had thought to go back to even scavenge the remains, but he, initially with the help of some of the children who had rescued him, stayed behind.
For the first few months, he was physically unable to move, or at least not without intense pain. His recovery saved him, but it wasn’t enough to restore him to his former self, and now that human magic had been sealed away, they couldn’t help him directly. In the months that followed, he gained some independence, but deeply affected by the war, he still needed help to function.
But the children grew up and had responsibilities of their own. Ant knew this and didn’t want to burden them with his situation, and when they eventually left him alone, he didn’t beg any of them to stay, as much as he wanted to. Still unable to let go of what little remained of his former life, he stayed behind to protect what was left of the village, thanks in part to what he had learned while traveling the world, and in part by raiding anyone who came too close.
summary: A take on Monster Tenna based on Undertale but set in a more modernized world.
title: Ant

content:
Catri#Catri is a darkner based on a well-loved GBA that’s originally Asriel’s, that got their battery lid lost and that’s been abandoned for a while now, gathering dust on a corner. She can display different faces depending on the cartridge she has in, but the cat-like faces are her default ones.
Personality#She’s very sweet and shy, but its not hard to make her open up to new people because she’s also quite approachable, just not the one to usually take the first step when getting to know new people. Basically, think of a shy but affectionate cat and that’s her. She’s passionate about videogames, but also has a lot of cat-like mannerisms, with an easy-going personality and a profound love for naps and good company. She takes waiting and not having any attention quite well though, as a handheld she’s only played sparingly and is used to being left alone.
Storylines#Arcade!Catri (Her lore with Kayden)#This version of Catri got lost somewhere in hometown one day that Asriel took it with him to play outside. Years later Berdly finds the console, and seeing how dusty and dirty it was he brings it home to clean it up , keeping it once he sees it works and not taking her outside in case he looses it just like the previous owner, who he assumes he have it up for lost.
That’s when she’s integrated into Kayden’s team. He’s at first skittish of her, jealous of her capacity to be taken outside by the lightner to play games, but when he sees she’s kept at home with him he ends up recognising her abilities as a great playtester and rapidly becomes his right hand. However she sometimes gets on Kayden’s nerves as she works much more calmly than what he’d like, while Catri respects him as a boss but works only on her own terms, so they get along but aren’t really close friends.
Main#She’s somewhere lost within TV World, in a section that’s out of Tenna’s reach so she can’t really reach other darkners there, but because she believes Asriel will sometime come back to search for her she isn’t too discouraged about being lost. She’s glad she’s found by the fun gang as Susie ends up kind of “adopting” her, which really means that Kris lends the handheld console to her.
Mantle Game#Tenna quickly recognizes her use at working at games, both partaking as an NPC as to help build any section in them, though as she’s mostly working behind the scenes her presence is easily overlooked, however she does end up being a good friend of Ramb because of that same reason.
Ramb, in order to hide the original Mantle Game from Tenna, trusts on Catri’s to take good care of it. She’s not explained the importance of the game, and curiosity ends up getting the best of her and she tries to run it herself, an opportunity that friend takes to explore around in her body.
summary: A handheld console darkner. She’s just glad to have some attention, she doesn’t need much really.
title: Catri

content:
Concept#More than a “gameshow host” he’s a mix between a butler and the owner of an arcade, still a host but not as flashy. He has the responsibility of taking care of the “arcade machines” (which are the representations of many videogames) and he does so as a supervisor that has many employees that do the maintenance (he’s very involved in the inspection tho).
Lightworld#Kayden is a not-so-old and rather small TV that Berdly owns for retro gaming, but in the last years he’s been getting less and less attention since Berdly’s playing more on PC. Luckily for him, the town’s internet connection being down has put him back in the spotlight, and has to take the opportunity to avoid getting put aside once again.
Personality#His main objective and wish is to entertain the lightners. He’s also stuck to the past with nostalgia and is very weary of new technology.
While working#He love his job, specially when it comes to entertaining the lightners, he takes great pride on doing a great job, but at the same time he takes it too seriously and gets really angry the second something goes wrong, specially with his employees.
The first impression he gives off with lightners is that he is very helpful and professional, but also joyful, making dumb jokes and gigs here and there ensuring everyone’s having fun. He kind of has the humour of original Tenna but is much less frenetic. However he can be quite overbearing, as inside the videogames he puts for the lightners he’s always somewhere nearby, taking the role of a neutral NPC in shops, as a guide or even in the audience withing the game.
With his workers he’s a very strict boss, he doesn’t exploit them, but his obsession with perfection is often annoying, he hates any kind of error that makes a game not “perfect” in his eyes (except if a lightner enjoys it, in which case he relaxes about it a bit). Its the kind of boss that if he doesn’t like how you’re doing something prefers to do it himself, and in turn his employees barely have any work left to.
Under professional front he’s very sensitive, and overall he’s good at hiding that, but he gets envyous really easily, making up for it inflating his ego.
Outside of work#All that joy and cordiality is replaced by tiredness, but he’s still very prideful. He’s incapable of fully disconnecting from his job at any given time.
As he hides his frustration to keep a professional front during work, outside of it he’s has no patience left and has his true feelings much more exposed, being more rageful.
Relationships#Once you’ve earned his favour (specially if you’re not a worker of his or are a lightner), he’s very keen on helping out, but he’s otherwise a bit standoffish, having to really earn his trust to get him to open up and hang out. His main way of showing affection if through acts of service and kind words, but he really likes receiving physical affection, even though he (barely) tries to avoid it during work to stay professional.
His envy also applies to interpersonal relationships, getting easily angered if he feels left out and being quite jealous in romantic relationships.
Abilities#His main special ability is that he can put anyone and himself inside any videogame (8 or 16 bit) in any moment, but he only takes the role of a neutral NPC (in theory he could take any role, but doesn’t like to). He also can change his own and the environment’s sprites at will, just so he fits perfectly in any game.
When he doesn’t want to let fo of the lightners he locks them inside a videogame, but if he gets too angry he gets glitchy and breaks the games he’s in.
title: R. Kayden
